h: Divine Favor and the Sacred Speech of Shabbos

p: It is stated in Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 4):
and the mouth in the soul."
That is, the holiness of the Shabbos day
has its root in the letter
שֶׁהוּא מֵחוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
which belongs to the seal of HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
which is the first and last
and middle letter of the alphabet,
and therefore the opening of the Torah
from before the world was created,
for it preceded it by two thousand years,
"And I was His delight day by day";
that is, the aspect of Chochmah and Binah,
which precede the days of Creation;
for the Torah came forth from Chochmah.
alludes to the aspect of "will be,"
which is the aspect of the World to Come,
And the holiness of the Shabbos day
is a perception akin to the World to Come.
and they correspond to the three Shabbos meals.
is the aspect of the revelation of the kingship of Heaven,
corresponding to the meal of the night of holy Shabbos.
is the aspect of Ze'ir Anpin,
alludes to "will be," in the future;
the aspect of Atika shines forth.
And the aspect of chen, grace,
and it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 28:9):
and a thread of grace was drawn over her";
that is, not on account of beauty
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (שְׁמוֹת לג, טז)
And as it says of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him (Shemos 33:16):
that I have found grace in Your eyes,
כִּי אֵצֶל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
"And she saw him that he was good"
immediately at the time of his birth,
not on account of his own choice;
that is, on account of finding grace
in His eyes, may He be blessed.
And likewise the aspect of the holiness of Yisrael,
the people who survived the sword."
and they shall be My people."
And Chazal, of blessed memory, said (Kiddushin 70b):
for regarding Yisrael it is written,
and they shall be My people,'
whereas regarding converts it is written,
and I will be your God…'";
And this is only on account of finding grace
in His eyes, may He be blessed,
"Is not Esav a brother to Yaakov?
and as Chazal, of blessed memory, said (Gittin 57a):
the difference between a sinner of Yisrael
and the prophets of the nations of the world."
And the holiness of the Shabbos day
only on account of finding grace,
"The most desirable of days You called it"
"And God completed on the seventh day…,"

p: And the matter of the holiness of the mouth in the soul
as Chazal, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 99b)
"Could it mean the toil of labor?
When it says…" and so on;
"you must say: the toil of the mouth."
like the work of the Mishkan,
like the actual performance of mitzvos,
and also raising one's children to Torah study;
only the toil of the mouth:
to sanctify one's mouth with Torah and prayer.
And this is especially on the Shabbos day,
"If you restrain your foot because of Shabbos…
and it does not say "and from speaking of matters,"
as it says "from pursuing your affairs";
to hint that the essential holiness of the Shabbos day
is to speak words of holiness,
And it is stated in the Gemara
"That your speech on Shabbos should not be
like your speech on a weekday."
who would talk a great deal;
For from the Gemara there is no proof,
only that it should not be like your weekday speech,
meaning about labors forbidden on Shabbos;
and on this came the hint in the Midrash
that even all kinds of talk
out of a feeling for the holiness of Shabbos,
which is the holiness of the mouth,
because it is the ultimate purpose
of the creation of heaven and earth.
And Chazal, of blessed memory, said (Chullin 89a):
What should be a person's craft?
Let him make himself as if mute in this world.
Could this be even regarding words of Torah?
And at the end of the passage it says,
for the mouth of Hashem has spoken";
כִּי עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת פִּיו כָּאָמוּר
for through the holiness of his mouth, as said,
one comes to the delight that is in holiness,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רא, ב)
as stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 201b):
at the moment the day is sanctified,
דִּמְמַנָּא עַל כָּל שְׁאָר פּוּמִין וְכוּלֵּי
appointed over all the other mouths…" and so on,
"that which is called the mouth of Hashem…";
he said: I have kissed the mouth of Hashem…" and so on.
And from these words it appears
לֹא שָׁמַע מֵרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי
had not heard from Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai
rather, he sensed of his own accord
that he was the very mouth of Hashem,
the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos
as stated in the holy Zohar,
are like Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim.
And it is as it says in Yeshayahu (40:1–5):
A voice calls in the wilderness:
And the glory of Hashem shall be revealed…
for the mouth of Hashem has spoken."
And it is stated in the Pesikta (Nachamu)
that all the prophets comforted Yisrael
and they did not accept comfort,
שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
who spoke to them from the mouth of HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
did not the other prophets too
speak in the Name of Hashem?
is in the conclusion of the words:
even in a place desolate of people,
and who is the one calling?
Only that the glory of Hashem be revealed;
that the mouth of Hashem has spoken":
that is, that all these words
that are spoken in words of Torah and prayer
are truly the mouth of Hashem.
as stated in the sefer Noam Elimelech
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל (בְּרָכוֹת ז, א)
'And I will make them joyful in My house of prayer';
with the intent of the heart
like the matter of "If my prayer is fluent in my mouth" (Berachos 34b),
which is a term of sending;
for the soul senses in itself
were sent into his mouth from Above.
And therefore it is said with the Name Adnus,
which is from the aspect of fear:
that the King of the kings of kings,
and he has no movement at all in his mouth
apart from Him, may He be blessed.
to "And I will make them joyful in My house of prayer":
that he senses in his soul
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu is praying this;
and from this joy is born in the heart,
like the matter of "my joy out of my fear."
And also regarding words of Torah,
who sits and occupies himself with Torah…" and so on,
where I cause My Name to be mentioned…";
שֶׁהֵם שְׁמוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
which are the Names of HaKadosh Baruch Hu.
And it uses the term "I cause to be mentioned,"
Hashem Yisbarach sends into his mouth
and He is the One who mentions.
in the context of the offerings:
"An altar of earth you shall make for Me…
for the service of the offerings
who are the emissaries of the Merciful One;
and "for the sake of six things
for the sake of Hashem…" and so on (Zevachim 46b).
And this is "I cause My Name to be mentioned":
for he is only an emissary from Him, may He be blessed,
to mention His Name, may He be blessed.
And from this it is learned for one who occupies himself with Torah,
as if he offered all the offerings (Menachos 110a),
"This is the law of the burnt offering…"
